summary: Saburō Hasegawa studied at the University of Tokyo (~1926–1929). He taught Alan Watts and held teaching posts at the American Academy of Asian Studies and the California College of the Arts (~1955–1957).
Working in computational linguistics and Indology, Sachin Kathale earned an M.Phil. from Jawaharlal Nehru University in 2007 and served as a teacher at Samskrita Bharati.

Sadajiro Sugiura studied at Rikkyo University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Episcopal Divinity School. Active in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, he taught at Pennsylvania, the Army War College, and Rikkyo University, where he became professor emeritus.

Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Sadananda Das earned degrees from Central Sanskrit University and Savitribai Phule Pune University. In 2005, he was appointed lecturer at the University of Leipzig.
Saerji works in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. His career includes serving as associate professor and faculty member at Peking University, attested between 2010 and 2026.
Working in history, archaeology, Indology, and linguistics, Sagar Uday More earned MBBS and DNB degrees at Niga Hospital and became a member of the Epigraphical Society of India in 2025.
Sai Susarla works in computational fields and Indology. He served as dean at MIT World Peace University (attested 2019) and held a post at the Siddhanta Knowledge Foundation (attested 2025).

Sai Venkatesh Balasubramanian studied at Shanmugha Arts, Science, Technology & Research Academy (B.Tech, Ph.D.) and Assam Don Bosco University (MBA). He worked as a research and hardware engineer at IBM India (2011–2012).

Working in history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Said Reza Huseini studied at Jawaharlal Nehru University, Leiden University, King's College London, and the University of Cambridge.

Specializing in Indology and history, Saiyid Athar Abbas Rizvi studied at Dr. B. R. Ambedkar University under Mohammad Habib. He held posts at the University of Jammu and Kashmir, SOAS, JNU, and the Australian National University (1967–1986).
Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sakda Hemthep studied under Peter Harvey and Max Deeg at Cardiff University (M.Phil., 2014) and became a PhD researcher at Ghent University (attested 2026).
Active in religious studies, Sakunoshin Motoda studied at Kenyon College, the University of Pennsylvania, and Columbia University before holding a post at Rikkyo University (~1899–1923).
Specializing in Japanology and history, Sakutaro Fujioka studied at the University of Tokyo (~1894–1897) and subsequently held a post there from ~1900 to 1910.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khenpo Appey Rinpoche, and others. He founded Sakya Centre, Sakya College, and Sakya Institute, and served as Abbot of Sakya Monastery until 2017.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Sakyong Mipham studied at Oxford, Namdroling Monastery, and under Chögyam Trungpa, whom he succeeded. He also served on the board of Naropa University until 2018.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, religion, and philosophy, Sallie B. King studied under Leon Hurvitz at the University of British Columbia (~1973–1975) and served as Professor of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University (~1992).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman earned her PhD at UC Berkeley (1979), studying under Shivram Dattatray Joshi and T. Shrinivas Shastri. A scholar of Indology and linguistics, she had a long teaching career at UC Berkeley.

Specializing in Buddhist and religious studies, Sally McAra earned her MA at the University of Auckland (1999–2000) under Christine Dureau and Karen Nero, later becoming an honorary research fellow there in 2019.
Sally Mellick Cutler, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, earned her D.Phil. from the University of Oxford in 1993 and served as office manager of the Pali Text Society (attested 1996–1997).

Salome Zajadacz-Hastenrath was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She completed her studies at Pädagogische Akademie Aachen (1951–1953), the University of Bonn (1956), and the University of Cologne (PhD, 1956–1965).
